title: Microsoft Teams: report suspicious guest invitations to your admin
summary: The reporting controls, default and rollout window are supported, with no blocking findings. The claim that the rollout timeline moved more than once is unconfirmed; the licensing model, differing Defender licensing guidance and shortened report path also need small corrections.

claims.claim: Teams enables users to report unexpected invitations to join another organisation as a guest for IT review.
claims.quote: When users receive an unexpected or potentially malicious invitation to join another organization as a guest, they can report it to their IT admin for review

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe guest-invitation reporting itself.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams report suspicious guest invitations reporting security licensing AllowSecurityEndUserReporting; "Teams" "guest invitations" "report". Opened end-user-reporting-security, end-user-reported-security-signal and submissions-teams; no feature-specific description.

claims.claim: Learn has not explicitly confirmed the PowerShell parameter's coverage of guest invitations.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams report suspicious guest invitations reporting security licensing AllowSecurityEndUserReporting. Read Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy's AllowSecurityEndUserReporting and Identity sections and end-user-reporting-security; neither names guest invitations.

claims.claim: Analytics & reports > Protection reports > View reports > User reported security submissions reaches the report.
claims.quote: go to Analytics & reports > Protection reports. ... On the View reports tab, under Report, select User reported security submissions. ... Under Report category ... Under Date range ... Select Run report.
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].ui.path and its rendered path with 'Analytics & reports > Protection reports > View reports > Report > User reported security submissions > Report category > category > Date range > Run report', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/end-user-reported-security-signal.

claims.claim: No API for the Teams User reported security submissions report is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "User reported security submissions" "API"; Teams security submissions report Microsoft Graph beta PowerShell API. Read end-user-reported-security-signal, submissions-teams and Get-MgBetaSecurityThreatSubmission; no operation for this Teams report.

claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because Microsoft has not published a guest-invitation-reporting-specific requirement.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included'. Begin licensing.notes with 'Except for joining meetings anonymously, each user in your organisation needs a Microsoft Teams licence to use Teams; no requirement specific to guest-invitation reporting is published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access. Retain the uncertainty about Defender requirements.
